title: KAFKA-20338: Add JMH performance benchmarks for KafkaRaftClient
body: ## Background KafkaRaftClient implements KRaft, Kafka's Raft consensus protocol. Today a single KafkaRaftClientDriver thread repeatedly calls KafkaRaftClient#poll() and each poll() iteration is an "all-in-one" event handler: it updates state, sends/handles RPCs, appends records (on the leader), and updates listeners to the log. The Kafka metadata team plans to refactor this programming model so that each of those responsibilities becomes a distinct event scheduled on a single-threaded event queue, the model already used elsewhere in Kafka (e.g. the controller's event queue). The raft module has strong correctness protection (unit tests and simulation tests), but it has no performance benchmarks.A refactor of this size to a layer this critical can silently regress performance This PR adds a protocol-level JMH benchmark suite. ## What changed Each benchmark follows the shape state X -> event -> state Y and reuses the existing RaftClientTestContext fixture. ### This first PR covers: - ElectionBenchmarks : a full Unattached → Leader election (electLeader), @Param voter count {3, 5}. To make a state-consuming election repeatable under AverageTime, each invocation drives Unattached → Leader and then resigns back to Unattached (via a higher observed epoch), so one context serves every invocation. - LeaderBenchmarks : steady-state leader request handling against one prepared leader : a caught-up FETCH that does not advance the high watermark, a FETCH from a follower that is behind, and a DESCRIBE_QUORUM admin query. #### Parametrizing scenarios (how to add a benchmark): For the RPC request-handling benchmarks (LeaderBenchmarks), related scenarios are not separate methods. A scenario is a constant in an enum that implements ParameterizedRpc, and JMH's @Param sweeps every constant, producing one result row (and one regression baseline) per scenario. Each constant carries: - a build(...) factory that constructs the inbound request for that scenario, and - the request/response API keys it expects to still be in-flight when the invocation ends (the harness drains exactly those and fails if anything else remains). Adding a scenario means adding a constant. ## Run with: Run individually: ./jmh-benchmarks/jmh.sh BenchmarkClassName Run all: ./jmh-benchmarks/jmh.sh ".*jmh.raft.*" ## Testing Ran the suite locally and the work counters match the expected per-operation profiles. # Sample Output Leader benchmark output: 3 and 5 voter output for electLeader ElectionBenchmark: # Fixture optimizations The raft JMH benchmarks (KAFKA-20338, apache/kafka#22669) run a real `KafkaRaftClient` against the `RaftClientTestContext` mock fixture, driven on the benchmark thread. Because the fixture sits **inside** the measured region, unchecked fixture overhead can dominate the numbers and mask real regressions. The changes below drive that overhead down so the benchmark measures **KafkaRaftClient**: # Optimization Changes 1. Excluded log4j-slf4j-impl from the jmh runtime (build.gradle) slf4j falls back to its NOP provider, so LogContext uses its lazy, non-location-aware path and never toStrings log arguments. 2. Lazy assertion message in MockListener.handleLeaderChange assertTrue(cond, String) builds the message (a String.format) eagerly on every leader change; the Supplier overload defers it to the failure path. 3. Skip the request serialize/deserialize round-trip Benchmark contexts set `withBenchmarking(true)`; roundTripApiMessage then returns the message as-is. The round-trip is network-layer work outside raft/src/main, so it's excluded from the measured region. 4. Bounded poll instead of waitForCondition `TestUtils.waitForCondition` throws and catches an AssertionError on every unsatisfied poll; the bounded loop just polls and checks, with no exceptions. 5. MockLog scan flattening `read()`, `metadataForOffset`, and `endOffsetForEpoch` head-scanned the log O(n), and the cost grew as the iteration's log grew. Replaced with binary search (firstBatchEndingAtOrAfter, upper-bound search over epochStartOffsets). `initializeLeaderEpoch` replaced its full-list removeIf with an O(removed) tail-pop. 6. MockLog.endOffset() / startOffset() rewritten as branches Both computed one long through an Optional chain; orElse(...) evaluates its argument eagerly, so the unused snapshot fallback, including a TreeMap lookup, ran on every call. Rewritten as plain if/else. Reviewers: Kevin Wu , Jonah Hooper , Alyssa Huang , José Armando García Sancio

+package org.apache.kafka.jmh.raft;
+
+import org.apache.kafka.common.protocol.ApiKeys;
+import org.apache.kafka.common.protocol.ApiMessage;
+import org.apache.kafka.raft.RaftClientBenchmarkContext;
+
+import java.util.Optional;
+
+/**
+ * A single inbound-RPC scenario for the raft request-handling benchmarks: the request to deliver
+ * to the node under test, together with the RPCs the node should have left on its send queue once
+ * it has handled that request.
+ *
+ * Implementations of this interface are enums whose values represent different RPCs. A benchmark's
+ * {@code @State} class holds a JMH {@code @Param} field of the enum type, which parameterizes the
+ * same benchmark code over multiple RPCs: JMH runs the method once per constant, so every constant
+ * is its own result row and its own regression baseline, and adding a scenario means adding a
+ * constant.
+ *
+ * A benchmark times only the handling of the request: {@link #build} constructs the request in
+ * setup, outside the measured region. {@link #expectedResponse()} declares the response the node
+ * should produce; the harness verifies it and fails if the node left any request unanswered,
+ * catching an unintended extra RPC.
+ */
+public interface ParameterizedRpc {
+
+    ApiMessage build(RaftClientBenchmarkContext benchmark);
+
+    Optional<ApiKeys> expectedResponse();
+}
